messages:
Marta (customer): Hi team — after rotating our API key this morning our prod workers are getting 401 invalid_api_key for ~10% of requests. New key shows active in the console. Error started ~08:12 UTC. Any quick checks?
Erin (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the curl/headers you're using (sanitise the key)? Also is this across all regions or just a single cluster? :thinking:
Marta (customer): Single GKE cluster in us-west1. App pulls key from a KMS-sync job that writes to a Kubernetes secret; our rollout replaced envvars and pods. Curl we tried (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_NEWKEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'
```
Result: 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or revoked"}
Erin (support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) confirm the first 8 chars of the key in the console matches what your app actually has (list mask shows first/last few chars), 2) check for trailing newline/whitespace in the secret. Could you run `kubectl exec` into a pod and `echo -n "$MY_API_KEY" | xxd` or `printf '%s' "$MY_API_KEY" | wc -c`?
Marta (customer): Ran inside one failing pod. `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | wc -c` returns 40 (expected 44). Huh. Looks truncated.
Kai (eng): That explains intermittent 401s — some pods have full key, others truncated. Possible causes: secret sync job chunking, base64 decode bug, or env var length limit. Does your syncer write the secret as base64 or raw?
Marta (customer): Our KMS syncer decodes the plaintext then writes to the secret value via `kubectl create secret generic` (we run in a short-lived job). We added a small pipe that trims newlines earlier.
Erin (support): Can you share the exact command you use to write? A common pitfall is using `echo $KEY > file` (adds newline) then `base64` variations; also some CI runners wrap the value.
Marta (customer): We do `kms-decrypt | base64 -d > /tmp/keyfile && kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-file=key=/tmp/keyfile --namespace=prod --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`
Kai (eng): That should be fine normally. Two angles: 1) if `/tmp/keyfile` was created with truncated output (maybe kms-decrypt returned partial), or 2) the create-secret from-file path may be hitting a logger/truncation in the sync job. Another possibility: the k8s secret ends up split across multiple lines and your app's env var reader truncates at NUL/whitespace.
Sophia (security): Also confirm the old key was not revoked prematurely. If you rotated and revoked the previous key immediately, pods still running with the old (full) key should be fine until they reload. But partial keys won't match either.
Marta (customer): We rotated keys via the console and set the old key to disabled immediately. We did not revoke for compliance until later.
Erin (support): OK. Can we collect an example failing request header from your app logs (redact keys)? Also give me one working pod's key `echo -n $API_KEY | xxd` and a failing pod's same check.
Marta (customer): Attached.dump:
Working pod:
```
00000000: 4b65 793a 4131 4278 6a7a 4f5a 2d2d 2d2d  Key:A1BxjzOZ----
... (masked)
```
Failing pod:
```
00000000: 4b65 793a 4131 4278 6a7a 4f5a 2d2d      Key:A1BxjzOZ--
```
Shows two bytes missing at end.
Kai (eng): Looks like your sync job is intermittently truncating the file before create. Two suggested repros: 1) run your KMS job repeatedly and immediately run `kubectl get secret -o yaml` to inspect `data.key` base64 length, 2) add a post-sync checksum verification step: `sha256sum /tmp/keyfile` and compare to expected.
Erin (support): For immediate mitigation: restart the failing pods so they get a fresh secret mount (that should pull the full value if the secret is correct). As a safer rotation path, create the new secret with a different name and do a rolling update referencing the new secret, then delete the old secret after all pods are on the new one.
Marta (customer): Restarting fixed it for now — we did a `kubectl rollout restart` and errors dropped to 0. We'll patch our syncer with a write-then-rotate approach and a checksum.
Sophia (security): Follow-up: do not revoke the old key until your deployment window is complete. Also consider using our API key rotation endpoint to schedule a soft-rotate (it keeps a 10-minute grace binding old key to reduce outages).
Erin (support): Filing an internal follow-up for docs: add a short guide on "safe api key rotation" for customers using KMS-syncers and k8s secrets. Also will add a troubleshooting checklist: check secret length, echo -n, xxd, restart pods, check key masking in console.
DeployBot: new ticket created: SUP-4829 - "API key rotation mismatch causing intermittent 401s" assigned to eng oncall
Kai (eng): Notes for our runbook: 1) check admin /v1/keys log for lookup failures with request ids, 2) check our secret validation metric (we'll add metric for key lookup length mismatch), 3) consider adding a small delta in the rotation process to keep old key valid for 5-15m by default.
Marta (customer): Thanks everyone — really appreciate the quick help. We'll follow up once the syncer patch is in. :thumbsup:
